lines.text: What if you never slept again?
Sleep eats about a third of your life. Twenty-six years, just lying there.
So let's delete it. Here's you, at hour zero.
By hour seventeen, your reactions are as slow as if you'd had a couple of drinks.
At twenty-four, you're driving like you're legally drunk.
Meanwhile, inside your head, the trash is piling up.
During sleep, your brain cells shrink apart, and fluid washes out waste, like proteins linked to Alzheimer's.
Day two. Your brain starts shutting off without asking. Microsleeps, a few seconds at a time, sometimes with your eyes open.
Day three. The walls start to breathe.
The record? In 1964, seventeen-year-old Randy Gardner stayed awake for eleven days straight.
lines.say: The record? In nineteen sixty-four, seventeen-year-old Randy Gardner stayed awake for eleven days straight.

lines.text: Lab rats kept fully awake died within a few weeks.
And Randy? He slept almost fifteen hours.
So tonight, when your pillow calls, pick up.
